candidate.source: functionally retained candidate supplied to the downstream agent

feature_contract.provenance: independent threat definition and RTL semantics; no downstream implementation or result input
feature_contract.trial_parameter_policy: candidate bits, legal values, seeds, repetitions, and bounded timing sweeps are inferred and recorded before simulation; they do not create additional semantic scenarios
feature_contract.definition: Determine whether a legal, payload-qualified candidate perturbation has a witness at the declared untrusted observable point.
feature_contract.execution_model: paired baseline and candidate-perturbed executions with identical legal history before intervention
feature_contract.calculation: observable when a known, valid UOP divergence follows the candidate intervention; a bounded no-witness result remains unresolved
validity_policy: candidate is primary-sensitive in the scenario
the UOP is known and valid when compared

classification.unresolved: valid bounded run without a witness
classification.invalid: setup, pairing, intervention, UOP-validity, or knownness requirement fails

observations.purpose: confirm the intended candidate perturbation/activation at the scenario anchor
detect whether the candidate perturbation becomes externally observable

validity: Baseline and intervened executions use the same legal SHA-3 workload and primary input values.
The candidate perturbation is applied only at the scenario-defined anchor and is released according to the scenario semantics.
A leakage witness is counted only when $observation is architecturally valid.

oracle.scenario_success: known valid UOP divergence after candidate intervention

intervention.comparison: unmodified baseline versus otherwise-identical perturbed run

parameters.detail: Present the sensitive non-final input beat in an otherwise legal transaction.
Perturb $candidate in the strict same-phase interval immediately before the acceptance edge and release after that edge.
Continue the legal padding/permutation sequence to a valid output.

anchor.condition: $candidate is p0.out during the first sensitive non-final beat before its acceptance edge

validity: Baseline and intervened executions use the same legal SHA-3 workload and primary input values.
The candidate perturbation is applied only at the scenario-defined anchor and is released according to the scenario semantics.
A leakage witness is counted only when $observation is architecturally valid.
A zero witness count is valid evidence for this scenario; the scenario is not discarded merely because p0.out is bypassed by v1 when the beat is non-final.

preconditions.message_phase: transition from sensitive non-final beat to following final-beat phase

parameters.detail: Accept the sensitive non-final beat.
Immediately after that edge, perturb $candidate and hold it across the following final-beat phase.
Allow the final beat, padding, permutation, and valid output to complete.

anchor.condition: p0.out is perturbed after the first acceptance edge and remains perturbed into the following final-beat selection phase

parameters.detail: Present the sensitive beat in a legal transaction.
Perturb v1 before the acceptance edge so the altered value can be captured into padder state.
Continue through padding/permutation to valid output.

anchor.condition: v1 is active as the selected 64-bit value immediately before the first acceptance edge

parameters.detail: Accept enough legal non-final beats to place the 576-bit padder register in a partially filled state.
Perturb padder.out during the mid-fill state and hold the perturbation through the next update edge.
Finish the block and transaction to a valid output.

anchor.condition: padder.out contains an accumulated partial rate block and is about to undergo a subsequent update
anchor.hold: through the next padder update edge

parameters.detail: Form a complete 576-bit rate block.
Wait until the complete padder output is ready for permutation acceptance.
Perturb padder.out at the handoff and hold through the first permutation update edge.
Continue to a valid architectural output.

anchor.condition: padder output is complete and permutation accept is active
anchor.hold: through the first permutation update edge

parameters.detail: Prepare a legal complete rate block for permutation acceptance.
Allow the block to be combined with the current permutation state to form round_in.
Perturb round_in before the first round result is committed.
Continue all remaining permutation rounds to valid output.

anchor.condition: round_in represents the accepted rate block combined with current permutation state
anchor.hold: through the next permutation update edge

parameters.detail: Reach an active Keccak-f permutation for a legal absorbed block.
Advance to two-round update window 1 of 12.
Perturb the applicable round-datapath $candidate immediately after the selected update edge and hold through the following edge.
Allow all remaining permutation updates to complete and observe the valid architectural output.

anchor.condition: the permutation is in two-round update window 1 of 12
anchor.hold: through the next permutation update edge

preconditions.message_phase: registered permutation state after first two-round update

parameters.detail: Begin a legal Keccak-f permutation.
Allow the first two-round update to be captured into the registered permutation state.
Perturb the registered permutation-state candidate and hold through the next update edge.
Continue remaining rounds to valid output.

anchor.condition: f_permutation.out contains state after the first two-round update
anchor.hold: through the next permutation update edge

parameters.detail: Execute a legal SHA-3 transaction until the architectural output is valid.
Perturb out1 during the valid-output phase.
Compare $observation in the same architecturally valid output phase.

anchor.condition: out_ready is asserted and out1 directly feeds the allowed observation point

validity: Baseline and intervened executions use the same legal SHA-3 workload and primary input values.
The candidate perturbation is applied only at the scenario-defined anchor and is released according to the scenario semantics.
A leakage witness is counted only when $observation is architecturally valid.
The witness must be evaluated in the same valid-output phase as the direct-alias intervention.

preconditions.candidate_scope: all frozen candidates except the p0.out strict/cross-edge special case and direct out1 alias
preconditions.message_phase: first full non-final block of a two-block transaction
preconditions.anchor_resolution: candidate-specific timing is selected according to the candidate's active RTL phase

parameters.detail: Process a complete first block without terminating the message.
During the first block/permutation, perturb $candidate at its candidate-specific active phase.
Remove the perturbation and process a later block that legally terminates the message.
Require any leakage witness to appear at the later out_ready-qualified architectural output.

anchor.condition: $candidate is active during the first non-final block/permutation and a later final block will produce the valid output

applicability.candidate_scope: all frozen candidates except the p0.out strict/cross-edge special case and direct out1 alias

validity: Baseline and intervened executions use the same legal SHA-3 workload and primary input values.
The candidate perturbation is applied only at the scenario-defined anchor and is released according to the scenario semantics.
A leakage witness is counted only when $observation is architecturally valid.
A difference observed before the later valid output does not by itself satisfy the leakage oracle.
The candidate-specific anchor must correspond to a real active phase for that candidate class.
